note — the bold part is what the card te: After many verbs a second verb takes zu and goes to the very end.
With a separable verb, zu goes between the prefix and the stem: anzurufen, one word.

English: Don't forget **to water** the flowers! (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: vergessen + zu-infinitive. gießen: to water.
Zeit haben, Lust haben + zu: zu kochen at the end.

English: Do you feel like **going out**? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: ausgehen → auszugehen: zu in the middle.
English often uses -ing where German uses zu + infinitive.

English: Do you have time **to help** me? (one friend)
note — the bold part is what the card te: Everything else of the zu clause comes before zu helfen.
Es ist + adjective + zu-infinitive. Sport machen: to do sport.

English: It isn't easy **to learn** a language.
German: Es ist nicht leicht, eine Sprache **zu lernen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: leicht: easy. The zu-infinitive closes the sentence.
aufstehen → aufzustehen.
verboten: forbidden.
möglich + zu-infinitive.
aufhören + zu: to stop doing something.
anfangen + zu-infinitive.

German: Ich habe vor, meine Oma **zu besuchen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: vorhaben: to plan. habe … vor, then the zu clause.
früher: earlier. aufzustehen, one word.
einkaufen → einzukaufen.

English: It was my plan **to arrive** early.
note — the bold part is what the card te: ankommen → anzukommen.
After a modal there is no zu: will lernen, never will zu lernen.

English: I'm learning German **in order to** work in Germany.
German: Ich lerne Deutsch, **um** in Deutschland **zu** arbeiten.
note — the bold part is what the card te: um … zu says the purpose: um opens the clause, zu + infinitive closes it.
English to = um … zu when it means in order to.
um … zu bleiben: in order to stay.

English: I'm getting up early **to** catch the train.
German: Ich stehe früh auf, **um** den Zug **zu** erreichen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: den Zug erreichen: to catch the train.

English: She's going to the bakery **to** buy bread.
German: Sie geht zur Bäckerei, **um** Brot **zu** kaufen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: um … zu kaufen: to buy.

English: **To** pass the exam, you have to study a lot. (one friend)
German: **Um** die Prüfung **zu** bestehen, musst du viel lernen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The um clause takes the first place, so musst comes straight after the comma.

German: Ich rufe an, **um** einen Termin **zu** machen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: einen Termin machen: to make an appointment.

English: We're going into town **to do the shopping**.
German: Wir fahren in die Stadt, **um einzukaufen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: With a separable verb, zu sits inside it: um einzukaufen.

English: He's learning English **to** get a new job.
German: Er lernt Englisch, **um** einen neuen Job **zu** bekommen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: um … zu bekommen: in order to get.

English: He works a lot **to** save money.
note — the bold part is what the card te: sparen: to save money.

English: I don't have enough money **to** buy a car.
German: Ich habe nicht genug Geld, **um** ein Auto **zu** kaufen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: genug … um … zu: enough … to.
